title: Affine attracting cells at rational isolated fixed points over an arbitrary field
statement:
Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $X$ be a nonempty smooth projective geometrically connected $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-projective-morphism, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Suppose $\mathbf G_{m,F}$ acts on $X$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; an action is a morphism $\mathbf G_m\times_F X\to X$ satisfying the unit and associativity identities. Assume there is an equivariant closed immersion $X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ for a nonzero finite-dimensional rational $\mathbf G_m$-representation $E$, meaning a group-scheme homomorphism $\mathbf G_m\to\operatorname{GL}(E)$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]; $\mathbf P(E)$ parametrizes lines and equivariance is an equality on every test algebra. Suppose the fixed subfunctor, consisting of points fixed after every algebra extension, is represented by a finite disjoint union $X^{\mathbf G_m}=\coprod_{a\in I}\operatorname{Spec}F$ of reduced $F$-points $x_a$. Then for each $a$ the functor
$$A\longmapsto\{f:\mathbf A^1_A\to X_A:\ f(tu)=t\cdot f(u)\text{ on all test }A\text{-algebras},\ f(0)=x_{a,A}\}$$
is represented, by evaluation at $1$, by a smooth locally closed subscheme $X_a^+\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space]. Here $\mathbf G_m$ acts on $\mathbf A^1$ by multiplication. These subschemes give a disjoint partition of the underlying topological space of $X$, and each $X_a^+$ is $F$-isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^{d_a}$ for some integer $d_a\geq0$. There is exactly one $a_0$ for which $X_{a_0}^+$ is open dense; no other stratum has closure $X$. For every field extension $L/F$ [def-pc-field-extension], the fixed subscheme of $X_L$ is the same disjoint union of $L$-points, and the attracting subscheme at $x_{a,L}$ is $(X_a^+)_L$; the partition, affine-space descriptions and distinguished open dense stratum persist. If $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$, its sole stratum is $\mathbf A_F^0$.

source.place: Theorem 13.47 and Corollary 13.49, printed pp.272--274, and the linear-action application after Lemma 13.51, p.275. Retain projectivity so that every geometric orbit has a limit, and require the fixed points to be rational, so that the affine fibres are affine spaces over F itself. The all-test-algebra formulation is the concentrator construction of Section 13g; its representing functor specifies the scalar-extension compatibility. This is the arbitrary-field form of the existing algebraically-closed-field lemma lem-sfb-projective-attracting-cells.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] over $F$ to choose coordinates $z_i$ with $t[z_i]=[t^{a_i}z_i]$. The chart $D_+(z_i)$ is affine with coordinates $u_j=z_j/z_i$ by [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], after relabelling the distinguished coordinate. Its weights are $a_j-a_i$, so it is invariant. Its intersection $U_i$ with $X$ is affine by [def-weil-closed-immersion], and smooth over $F$ by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Fix $x_a$, choose $i$ with $z_i(x_a)\ne0$, and put $w=a_i$, $c_j=u_j(x_a)$. Fixedness on every test algebra implies $c_j=0$ whenever $a_j\ne w$, by comparing Laurent monomials. Inside this chart let $C_a$ be defined by $u_j=0$ for $a_j<w$ and $u_j=c_j$ for $a_j=w$. It is an affine space on the remaining, strictly positive-weight coordinates. Define $Y_a=X\cap C_a$ scheme-theoretically inside $U_i$.

source.place: Lemma 13.46, p.272; Proposition 13.18 and Definition 13.21, pp.259--261.

proof.text: For an $F$-algebra $A$, the orbit of $y\in U_i(A)$ has ratios $t^{a_j-w}u_j(y)$. It extends in $U_i$ to $\mathbf A^1_A$ with value $x_{a,A}$ at zero exactly when the equations of $C_a$ hold. This coefficient comparison is valid for nonreduced $A$: $A[t]\to A[t,t^{-1}]$ is injective. Conversely those equations give the extension by this same polynomial formula; it lands in $X$ because its defining equations vanish after inverting $t$, hence already in $A[t]$. Thus $Y_a$ is the affine concentrator $U_i(\{x_a\})$. The point $\{x_a\}=\operatorname{Spec}F$ is an invariant smooth closed subscheme of $U_i$ (a rational point in this affine chart is cut out by its coordinate values). Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-concentrator] to conclude that $Y_a$ is smooth and closed in $U_i$, hence locally closed in $X$. The polynomial extension is equivariant: substituting $su$ for $u$ multiplies each positive-weight coordinate by $s^{a_j-w}$.

source.place: Definition 13.21 and Propositions 13.23--13.24, pp.261--262; Remark 13.57, p.277.

proof.text: An arbitrary equivariant $f:\mathbf A^1_A\to X_A$ with $f(0)=x_{a,A}$ factors through $(U_i)_A$. Indeed, on each geometric fibre the inverse image of the invariant closed complement is a closed invariant subset of $\mathbf A^1$ missing zero. If it contained a nonzero point, invariance would give the whole multiplicative orbit, whose closure contains zero. Thus it is empty on every geometric fibre, hence empty. The open factorization is provided by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]. In the affine chart, equivariance determines $f$ on $\mathbf G_{m,A}$ by $f(1)$, and injectivity of $A[t]\to A[t,t^{-1}]$ determines it everywhere. Step 2 now identifies evaluation at $1$ with a natural bijection between the functor in the statement and $Y_a(A)$. This proves representability, including nilpotent test algebras, and independence of the chosen chart, since each chart construction represents this identical functor over $X$. Set $X_a^+=Y_a$.

source.place: Remark 13.57 and the invariant-affine-open construction in Proposition 13.58, pp.277--278.

proof.text: Let $B=\mathcal O(Y_a)$. It is a quotient of the polynomial algebra of $C_a$, with its variables in strictly positive degrees. Its defining ideal is homogeneous: stability under the action is an identity of coactions, and comparing coefficients of $t$ in the quotient tensored with $F[t,t^{-1}]$ shows that each homogeneous component of an element of the ideal is again in the ideal. Hence $B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}B_n$, and $B_0=F$: evaluation at $x_a$ shows that no nonzero constant is killed. The maximal ideal of $x_a$ is $\mathfrak m=\bigoplus_{n>0}B_n$. Smoothness from Step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] imply that $B_{\mathfrak m}$ is regular. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-graded-regular-polynomial], including its existence of homogeneous cotangent-basis lifts, to obtain $B\simeq F[T_1,\ldots,T_{d_a}]$. By [def-sbc-affine-space] this gives $X_a^+\simeq\mathbf A_F^{d_a}$, with $d_a\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma 13.39, pp.268--269, and the polynomial-algebra argument of Theorem 13.44, pp.271--272.

proof.text:
For every algebraically closed extension $K/F$ and $y=[v]\in X(K)$, write $v=\sum_b v_b$ by weights and let $w$ be the least weight with $v_w\ne0$. Then
$$u\longmapsto[\sum_{b\ge w}u^{b-w}v_b]$$
is regular on $\mathbf A^1_K$: a nonzero weight-$w$ coordinate is constant and supplies a standard chart. Its equations for $X$ vanish after inverting $u$ and therefore in $K[u]$. At zero its value is the fixed point $[v_w]$, which must be one of the $x_{a,K}$. This last assertion is functorial fixedness, since $v_w$ lies in one weight space. Step 3 places $y$ in $X_a^+(K)$. The minimum-weight expression determines the limit uniquely, so no two cells meet on these points. Every scheme point lifts to an algebraic closure of its residue field; consequently the cells exhaust $|X|$ and their underlying subsets are pairwise disjoint. In particular $I$ is nonempty. Projectivity enters here as the given closed embedding: the explicit projective limit stays in $X$.

source.place: Proposition 13.20, pp.259--260; Theorem 13.47(c), p.273, used here with the explicit projective limit rather than an exhaustion claim without properness.

proof.text: The scheme $X$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] and connected by the hypothesis of geometric connectedness. By [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral], it is integral and thus irreducible and reduced. The finitely many closures of the cells cover $X$, so irreducibility forces one cell to have closure $X$. A dense locally closed subset is open: writing it as $V\cap Z$ with $V$ open and $Z$ closed, density gives $Z=X$. Two dense cells would therefore be disjoint nonempty opens of an irreducible space, impossible. The cell structure on this open subset is the open subscheme structure: both it and $X$ are reduced, and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], on an open where the cell is closed, identifies their ideals with the unique radical ideal defining the common support. This proves the unique open dense stratum and excludes every other stratum from having closure $X$.

source.place: Corollary 13.49(c) and its finite-partition argument, pp.273--274; regularity/integrality input: Stacks Tags 056S, 0569, 033N.

proof.text: Let $L/F$ be any field extension. For an $L$-algebra $A$, the conditions defining fixedness are exactly the original conditions for the same $F$-algebra $A$, since all further $A$-algebras are also $L$-algebras. Thus the fixed subfunctor is represented by $\coprod_a\operatorname{Spec}L$. Likewise the equations defining $Y_a$ become the identical equations with coefficients in $L$; equivalently the representing bijections of Step 3 apply to every $L$-algebra. They identify the attracting subscheme with $(X_a^+)_L$. The isomorphism of Step 4 becomes $L[T_1,\ldots,T_{d_a}]\simeq B\otimes_FL$, so it is still an affine space. The minimum-weight argument of Step 5 works over algebraic closures of residue fields of $X_L$, giving the same disjoint partition. To check density, $X_L$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-scheme-lfp-smooth-flat-base-change] and [lem-pc-field-extension-flat] (smoothness includes local finite presentation), and connected by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. It is nonempty since it contains $x_{a,L}$. The regularity and integrality nodes used in Step 6 therefore show $X_L$ is irreducible. The original open cell remains open by the inverse-image definition of base change of an open subscheme and nonempty because it contains $x_{a_0,L}$; hence it is dense, and the disjoint-partition argument again makes it unique. Finally, for $X=\operatorname{Spec}F$ the only possible $f$ is the structure map, the action is trivial, and the sole representing scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}F=\mathbf A_F^0$ by [def-sbc-affine-space].

source.place: Proposition 13.23 (field-extension compatibility), p.261, and the concentrator functor in Section 13g, pp.276--278; Stacks Tag 02V4 for smoothness after field extension.
